name: Four Categories of Oaths (Arba Shevuot)
notes: The Mishnaic framework of four oath types: future positive, future negative, past positive, past negative — foundational structure of tractate Shevuot

name: Oath Taken in Vain (Shevuat Shav)
notes: Oath about something impossible or obviously false, or oath to violate a commandment; distinct from shevuat sheker (false oath) — treated in Shevuot ch. 3

name: Oath on an Utterance (Shevuat Bitui)
notes: Oath to do or refrain from doing something in the future, or affirming/denying something about the past; primary category in Shevuot ch. 3

name: Oath of Testimony (Shevuat Edut)
notes: Oath taken by witnesses falsely denying knowledge of testimony; special rules re: who can administer it, liability, and sliding-scale offering — Shevuot ch. 4

name: Oath on a Deposit (Shevuat Pikadon)
notes: Oath falsely denying possession of another's deposit, loan, pledge, or stolen/lost item; requires guilt-offering and repayment with fifth — Shevuot ch. 5

name: Awareness of Impurity in Defiling Temple or Sacrificial Food (Yediot HaTumah)
notes: Detailed rules about whether awareness existed at beginning/end of transgression and how this affects liability for sliding-scale offering — Shevuot ch. 1-2

name: Atonement of Inner and Outer Yom Kippur Goats
notes: Distinction between the goat whose blood is presented inside (atones for awareness at beginning) vs. outside Sanctuary (atones for awareness at end) — Shevuot ch. 1-2

name: Atonement of Festival and New Moon Goats
notes: Dispute among R. Meir, R. Yehuda, and R. Shimon about which sins the goats of Rosh Chodesh and Yom Tov atone for — Shevuot ch. 1

name: Expansion of the Temple Courtyard (Tosefet Azarah)
notes: Procedure for consecrating additions to the Temple courtyard requiring king, prophet, Urim veTummim, Sanhedrin, two thanks-offerings, and song — Shevuot 2:2

name: Oath of Testimony — Court vs. Outside Court
hebrew: שבועת עדות בבית דין ושלא בבית דין
notes: Dispute whether witnesses become liable only when denying testimony in court or also outside court — Shevuot 4:1, 4:3

name: Oath of Testimony Limited to Monetary Claims
notes: Oath of testimony applies only where testimony would generate monetary liability; exempt for capital cases, fines, status claims — Shevuot 4:6-4:7

name: Partial Admission Oath (Modeh beMiktzat — Shevuot)
notes: Detailed rules of partial admission oath: minimum claim amount (two ma'ah), minimum admission (one peruta), same-type requirement — Shevuot ch. 6

name: Rabbinically Imposed Oath — Claimant Takes Oath and Collects (Shevuat HeSset/Takkanat Chachamim)
notes: Rabbinic enactment where plaintiff (not defendant) takes oath and collects: hired worker, robbery victim, injured party, opponent of oath-suspect — Shevuot ch. 7

name: Person Suspected of Taking False Oaths (Chashud al HaShevuah)
notes: When one litigant is disqualified from taking an oath due to prior false oaths, the opposing party takes the oath and collects — Shevuot 7:4

name: Oath of Partners and Managers (Shevuat Shutafin)
notes: Partners, sharecroppers, stewards, and household managers can be required to take oaths even without specific claims — Shevuot 7:8

name: Oaths of the Four Bailees (Shevuot Arba Shomrim)
notes: Detailed rules of what oath each of the four bailees takes and when; principle that oath stringent on defendant is exempt, lenient is liable — Shevuot ch. 8

name: Changing One's Claim (Shinui be'Tevi'ah) — Bailee Oaths
notes: Principle: bailee who changes from one claim of liability to another, or from exemption to liability, affects guilt-offering liability — Shevuot 8:2-8:6

name: Oath Administered Using Divine Names and Appellations
notes: Dispute between R. Meir and Rabbis whether oaths and curses using divine appellations (not Tetragrammaton) generate liability — Shevuot 4:13

name: Oath of Testimony Not Applicable to Fines (Kenas)
notes: One who denies a fine (double payment, four/five-fold, rape fine) is exempt from false oath offering since fines are not paid on self-admission — Shevuot 5:5

name: Dispute Over Value of Lost Collateral (Mashkon)
notes: Special rules when creditor and debtor dispute the value of collateral that was lost; who takes the oath — Shevuot 6:7

name: Storekeeper's Ledger Oath (Shevuat Chanvani al Pinkaso)
notes: Rabbinic enactment allowing storekeeper to take oath and collect when employer sent workers to receive goods — Shevuot 7:5-7:6

name: Land (Real Property) Not Subject to Oaths or Double Payment
notes: Land, documents, Canaanite slaves, and consecrated property are exempt from oaths, double payment, and bailees' liability — Shevuot 6:5

name: Oath to Perform or Refrain from a Mitzvah — Exempt
notes: One who swears to perform or not perform a mitzvah is exempt from sliding-scale offering for violation; dispute with R. Yehuda ben Beteira — Shevuot 3:6

name: Prohibition Cannot Take Effect Where One Already Exists — Oaths
notes: Applied to oaths: repeated oaths on same act generate only one liability; also applied to oath over already-prohibited foods — Shevuot 3:4, 3:7
